chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them:

About a man who entered into a mukātabah contract with his slave, and after making the contract he said: "Gift to me part of my mukātabah payment, and I will expedite your mukātabah payment." Is that permissible?
He said: "If it is a gift, then there is no harm. But if he says, ‘Reduce it from me and I will expedite it for you,’ then it is not proper."

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection in it
key_terms.فَلَا يَصْلُحُ: it is not valid or proper
key_terms.كَاتَبَ: he entered into a mukātabah contract of emancipation
key_terms.هِبَةً: a gift given voluntarily without compensation

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to reduce a mukātabah payment in exchange for early payment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a mukātabah contract between a master and a slave. It distinguishes between a voluntary gift or remission, which is allowed, and a negotiated reduction in exchange for earlier payment, which is not permitted.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3472 - Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as), about a man who entered into a mukataba (a contract of emancipation) with his slave.
After the contract, the slave said: "Forgive me part of my payments, and I will pay off the remainder early."
Imam (as) said: "If it is given as a gift, then there is no harm. But if he says, 'Reduce my payment in exchange for early payment,' then it is not permissible."
